question.worked_solution:
Recall that by definition, $\text{nullity}(D)=\text{dim}(\text{Null}(D)).$

To find $\text{dim}(\text{Null}(D))$, we reduce $D$ to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 5 & -7 & 9 \\ -3 & 6 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-5){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 9 \\ -3 & 6 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix has $3$ pivot columns and no non-pivot columns. 

Therefore,

$$
\text{nullity}(D)=\text{dim}(\text{Null}(D))=0.
$$
